original_question: Mutations in the gene that encodes transcription factor FKH-14 cause a second set of which anatomical feature?

final_qi.question: Mutations in the gene that encodes transcription factor FKH-14 cause a second set of which anatomical feature?
final_qi.long_answer: FOXC2, historically designated transcription factor FKH-14, is a forkhead family gene. Heterozygous FOXC2 mutations produce the lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome, whose characteristic feature is distichiasis—a second (accessory) row of eyelashes developing along the eyelid margin.

final_answer.long_answer: The gene FOXC2 (also known as forkhead transcription factor FKH-14) encodes a forkhead box transcription factor. Pathogenic FOXC2/​FKH-14 mutations cause lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome, whose defining ocular feature is distichiasis—a second row of eyelashes arising from the Meibomian glands of the eyelid.
